title: Women of the Bible IQ
subtitle: How well do you know the women who shaped the story?

questions.text: Who was the first woman, created by God in the garden?

options.explanation: Sarah was Abraham's wife, generations later. She is honored, but she was not the first woman.
Genesis names her Eve because she was "the mother of all living." She was formed from Adam's side in the garden.
Hagar was Sarah's servant and the mother of Ishmael, but not the first woman.
Rebekah was Isaac's wife, much later in Genesis.

questions.text: Which woman left her people, saying "thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God"?

options.explanation: Naomi was the older woman these words were spoken to. Her daughter-in-law said them as she chose to stay.
Orpah turned back to her own people, while the other daughter-in-law stayed.
Ruth the Moabite said this to Naomi in Ruth 1:16. She later married Boaz and became an ancestor of King David.
Esther's story is set in Persia, in a different book entirely.

questions.text: Which queen risked her life to save the Jewish people from Haman's plot?

options.explanation: Esther approached the king uninvited, knowing it could cost her life, and exposed Haman's plan. Her famous line is "if I perish, I perish."
Jezebel was a queen who opposed God's prophets, the opposite of a deliverer.
Bathsheba was the mother of Solomon, but she is not the one who faced down Haman.
Vashti was the queen before Esther, removed for refusing the king's command.

questions.text: Which woman was a judge and prophetess who led Israel into battle with Barak?

options.explanation: Miriam was a prophetess and Moses' sister, but she did not lead Israel as a judge.
Deborah judged Israel and summoned Barak to fight Sisera. She told him the honor of victory would go to a woman.
Huldah was a prophetess in the days of King Josiah, but she was not a judge who went to war.
Hannah was the mother of Samuel, known for her prayer, not for leading armies.

questions.text: Who drove a tent peg through the temple of the enemy commander Sisera?

options.explanation: In Judges 4, Jael welcomed Sisera into her tent, then drove a peg through his head while he slept, fulfilling Deborah's word.
Rahab hid the spies in Jericho, a different act of courage.
Delilah betrayed Samson by uncovering the secret of his strength, but she did not kill Sisera.
Abigail calmed David's anger with wisdom and gifts. Her story is a different one.

questions.text: Which woman of Jericho hid the Israelite spies and was later spared?

options.explanation: Rahab hid the two spies and let them down by a cord. A scarlet rope in her window marked her house to be spared. She is even listed in Jesus' family line.
There are women named Tamar in Scripture, but none of them hid the spies at Jericho.
Dinah was a daughter of Jacob, from an earlier story in Genesis.
Zipporah was the wife of Moses, not connected to Jericho.

questions.text: Who was the mother of Samuel, and prayed so earnestly that the priest thought she was drunk?

options.explanation: In 1 Samuel 1, Hannah prayed silently with moving lips. Eli thought she was drunk, but she was pouring out her heart for a son.
Peninnah was the other wife who provoked Hannah, not the praying mother.
Elizabeth was the mother of John the Baptist in the New Testament.
Rachel longed for children too, but she was the mother of Joseph and Benjamin, not Samuel.

questions.text: Which sisters were close friends of Jesus, one busy serving while the other sat at His feet?

options.explanation: In Luke 10, Martha was busy with serving while Mary sat listening. Jesus said Mary had chosen the good part. They were sisters of Lazarus.
Leah and Rachel were sisters who married Jacob, far back in Genesis.
Mary and Elizabeth were relatives, not the two sisters at Bethany.
Priscilla and Lydia were faithful women in the early church, but they were not sisters of Lazarus.

questions.text: Who was the mother of Jesus?

options.explanation: Mary Magdalene was a devoted follower of Jesus and a witness to the resurrection, but she was not His mother.
The angel Gabriel told Mary she would bear a son and call Him Jesus. She was engaged to Joseph at the time.
Elizabeth was Mary's relative and the mother of John the Baptist.
Anna was the elderly prophetess who praised God when the baby Jesus was brought to the temple.

questions.text: Which woman was the first to see the risen Jesus on Easter morning?

options.explanation: Mary the mother of Jesus stood by the cross, but the Gospels name a different woman as the first to see Him risen.
In John 20, Mary Magdalene wept at the empty tomb and met Jesus, at first thinking He was the gardener. He sent her to tell the others.
Joanna was among the women at the tomb, but Mary Magdalene is the one named meeting Jesus first.
Salome came with spices to the tomb, but she was not the first to see the risen Lord.

questions.text: Which businesswoman, a seller of purple cloth, became one of the first believers in Philippi?

options.explanation: Dorcas, also called Tabitha, was known for making clothes for the poor and was raised by Peter. She lived in Joppa, not Philippi.
Acts 16 introduces Lydia, a seller of purple from Thyatira. The Lord opened her heart, and she and her household were baptized.
Phoebe was a servant of the church at Cenchrea whom Paul commended, but she was not the purple seller.
Priscilla, with her husband Aquila, taught Apollos. She was a tentmaker by trade, not a seller of purple.

scoring.perfectMessage: You know these women and their stories by heart!
